hints: Focus on which functional groups can be converted into a carboxylic acid in just one step under suitable conditions.
Remember that acid hydrolysis of a nitrile gives a carboxylic acid with exactly the same carbon skeleton, the $\text{-CN}$ carbon becomes the $\text{-COOH}$ carbon.
Count the carbons and match the branching, the starting nitrile must already look like 2-methylbutanoic acid but with $\text{-CN}$ in place of $\text{-COOH}$.
walkthrough:
**Draw the target product**

First, let's be clear what we need to make. 2-methylbutanoic acid is a 4-carbon chain with a methyl branch on C2 and a carboxylic acid group.

Structure:
$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)\text{COOH}$$

**Recall the one-step routes to acids**

The classic single-reagent route is hydrolysis of a nitrile with dilute aqueous acid and heat. The $\text{-C}\equiv\text{N}$ group becomes $\text{-COOH}$ with no change to the rest of the skeleton.

General reaction:
$$\text{R-C}\equiv\text{N} + 2\text{H}_2\text{O} \xrightarrow{\text{dil. HCl, heat}} \text{R-COOH} + \text{NH}_4^+$$

**Work backwards to find Y**

To get $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)\text{COOH}$, Y must be $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)\text{CN}$. That is 2-methylbutanenitrile, with the same 5 carbons in total and the same branching.

options.A: Incorrect. Pentan-2-one, $\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$, is a ketone. Ketones resist further oxidation under normal conditions and cannot be converted to a carboxylic acid with the same carbon number in one step.
options.B: Incorrect. 2-methylbutan-2-ol, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{C}(\text{OH})(\text{CH}_3)_2$, is a tertiary alcohol. Tertiary alcohols are not oxidised by acidified dichromate or manganate because there is no H on the carbon bearing the $\text{-OH}$ group.
options.C: Correct. 2-methylbutanenitrile, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)\text{CN}$, on boiling with dilute aqueous acid hydrolyses directly to 2-methylbutanoic acid, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)\text{COOH}$. The carbon skeleton is unchanged.
options.D: Incorrect. Methylpropanenitrile, $(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{CHCN}$, does hydrolyse to an acid, but it gives 2-methylpropanoic acid, $(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{CHCOOH}$. It has only 4 carbons in total, one carbon short of the required product.
